newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Aborigine charged with "pointing the bone" threat.
newsitem.headline: Aborigine charged with "pointing the bone" threat.

text.p: An Australian Aborigine appeared in court on Tuesday charged with attempting to extort A$10,000 (US$7,600) by threatening to "point the bone", or place a death curse, on an Australian comedian.
Aboriginal activist John Kelly also threatened to place a curse on the family of comedian Kevin Wilson, the Northern Territory Supreme Court in Darwin heard.

Kelly, 50, made the extortion attempt after he heard Wilson perform a song which contained the words "boong" and "coon" in 1994, saying Wilson was making jokes at the expense of Aborigines, the court heard.
Both words are derogatory terms for Aborigines.
Kelly and his manager, Darwin bookmaker Bryan Clark, both pleaded not guilty to making a demand with menaces to obtain A$10,000 in November 1994.
The court heard that Kelly initially lodged a complaint with the Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission against Wilson's song in 1994.
He then threatened on Darwin radio to "paint up and put a curse on" Wilson, the court herad.
Kelly's manager then telephoned Wilson's manager and initially asked for a new four-wheel drive vehicle, but later lowered the demand to A$10,000.
In a telephone conversation taped at the time, transcripts of which were tendered in court, Wilson's manager asked Clark: "If you get the money you won't point the bone at Kevin?"
"No pointing the bone, yeah," Clark replied.
